prompt:
The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

<profile>
  tan: 0.70
  gal: 0.30
</profile>

Below are two texts.

TEXT_G:
Scottish National Party Manifesto 2001 – Summary

We stand for Scotland. Electing SNP MPs is a vote for Independence, for completing the powers of the Scottish Parliament, and for MPs who always put Scotland first. The more SNP MPs, the stronger the mandate for a referendum; a majority would trigger it. Meanwhile, SNP MPs will press immediately for more powers, better deals, and protection from Westminster’s failings.

Independence vision: a just, caring, enterprising Scotland using normal powers every nation has—control of revenues, welfare and investment—to deliver world-class public services. We will harness Scotland’s wealth by creating a sovereign Scottish Fund for Future Generations from oil revenues, and a not-for-profit Scottish Trust for Public Investment to replace costly PFI/PPP and drive infrastructure renewal.

Constitution and democracy: an independent, written constitution with inclusive citizenship; the Queen retained as Head of State subject to referendum; proportional representation at all levels; cut quangos and make remaining ones accountable; strong, opportunity-rich civil service.

Education and young people: abolish tuition fees; rebuild maintenance support; establish an Education Convention; reduce P1–P3 class sizes to 18 in phases; end misleading league tables; refurbish schools via STPI; support McCrone; promote Gaelic medium education; embed anti-racism; improve inclusion and special needs support; votes at 16; strengthen children’s rights with a powerful Commissioner.

Jobs and economy: Scotland-specific strategy—massive infrastructure, broadband everywhere, and national reskilling; streamline enterprise agencies; market Scotland globally; overhaul tourism into a marketing-led, access-focused industry.

Fair work: devolve and improve the New Deal; raise the minimum wage to £4.36 for all ages, with small business support; guarantee union rights and back EU worker protections.

Environment and utilities: make Scotland a sustainability leader; oppose the UK climate levy’s damage to hydro; deliver a State of the Nation Environmental Audit and a National Environment Plan; 12% of energy and 25% of electricity from renewables by 2010; no new nuclear, lead in decommissioning; embed polluter pays and resource efficiency; reform water charges and governance, stop backdoor privatisation.

Health and care: take politics out of the NHS with a National Health Care Commission; end postcode treatment—HTBS rulings binding; free fruit in schools and healthier meals; free dental check-ups; freeze and review prescription charges; invest via STPI in equipment, cleaner hospitals, 1,500 more nurses, and halve waits; free personal care for all elderly people.

Europe and the world: Scotland in Europe—pro-subsidiarity, anti-superstate; euro only by consent when conditions fit; independence brings full EU representation. Remove Trident; oppose US missile defence; negotiate phased withdrawal from NATO’s nuclear structures; create a professional Scottish Defence Force; ethical defence exports. Build business-focused external offices; meet UN aid targets; cancel debt; untie aid.

Culture, sport and language: devolve broadcasting, secure a Scottish Six; focus sport on communities; reform arts funding, create a national theatre and Scottish Lottery; secure status for Gaelic and promote Scots.

Social justice, housing and equality: a national anti-poverty strategy; end asylum vouchers; transfer housing debt, invest without wholesale stock transfer; core fund the voluntary sector; tackle homelessness; strengthen equality and disability rights; tougher on drug dealers with Drug Courts.

Safety and justice: 1,000 more police; empower courts against youth offending with parental compensation orders; lifelong restrictions for high-risk sex offenders; speed cases; retain Scottish justice receipts in Scotland.

Tax, local government and rural Scotland: honest, transparent tax—comprehensive review with no overall rise without mandate; immediately cut fuel duty by 10p/gal funded by a new 5p band on income over £100k; review local government finance including local income tax; PR/STV for councils. Support rural services, cut fuel burdens, improve transport and digital access.

Agriculture, fisheries, land: post–foot-and-mouth strategy; fair EU playing field; compensated tie-ups and technical conservation; reform CFP with zonal councils; salmon farming inquiry; empower community buy-outs; national freshwater policy.

Pensions and social security: restore the earnings link, spread winter payments weekly; streamline benefit delivery, boost take-up; fairer disability and carers’ support; fix WFTC traps.

Transport: secure Scotland’s fair UK share; invest via STPI; regional transport authorities; public share in Railtrack; reopen and electrify priority lines; concessionary travel; targeted road upgrades; lower ferry fares and abolish Skye Bridge tolls; expand direct flights and cut airport costs.

TEXT_D:
Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2001 – Summary (ideological framing preserved)

Core purpose: Freedom, Justice, Honesty. An enabling, less intrusive state guarantees the essentials—good schools and hospitals, safe streets, reliable transport, decent pensions—so everyone can fulfil their potential. Fairness funds freedom, and green principles run through every policy.

Health
- Cut waiting times by expanding NHS capacity: 27,500 more nurses, 4,600 more doctors, 10,250 allied professionals, 10,000 beds; £1,000 annual uplift for the lowest‑paid NHS staff; free personal care for the elderly and long‑term patients.
- Shift to prevention: restore free dental and eye checks, invest in diagnostics and public health, greener homes and cleaner air.
- End the “postcode lottery” via a national Pharmaceutical Agency; establish Patient Care Guarantees, advocates, and no‑fault compensation; ban age discrimination; end mixed wards.
- Free professionals from central diktats.

Education, Skills and Work
- Honest funding: add 1p to the basic income tax rate to invest over £3bn annually.
- Smaller classes and more staff: primary class averages cut to 25; 5,000 extra secondary teachers; 40,000 classroom assistants; paid preparation time; scrap crude performance pay and SATs at 7; cut bureaucracy; richer books/ICT.
- Abolish university tuition fees; restore grants for the poorest; widen access and support staff.
- Lifelong learning entitlements; paid study leave for 16–24s; replace the New Deal with a flexible, universal job‑help guarantee.

Law, Order and Liberty
- 6,000 more police and 2,000 retained community officers; a Community Safety Force for nuisance crime; independent police complaints; evidence‑led “stop and search.”
- Be tough and effective: more prevention, rehabilitation and community sentences; work and skills in prisons; reduce reoffending.
- Uphold rights: victim statements; end blanket mandatory sentences; protect jury trial and right to silence; liberalise licensing; civil penalties, not criminalisation, for TV licence non‑payment.

Transport
- Integrated, affordable, cleaner travel: free off‑peak buses for pensioners/disabled; aim half‑fares for under‑19s; greener VED with no real‑terms fuel duty rise.
- Empower councils (bonds, congestion charging) to fund better buses, trams, cycling and reopened rail.
- Stronger public control: a Sustainable Transport Authority; restructure Railtrack into a public‑interest model; rural transport fund; a 40% cut in road deaths/serious injuries target.

Pensions, Low Pay and Welfare
- Immediate pension boosts (more for over‑75s/80s), funded by a new 50p rate over £100,000; Independent Pensions Authority; toward citizen‑owned second pensions; end punitive means‑testing traps.
- Annual minimum wage review (single adult rate from 16+); extra help for children in long‑term poverty; fairer support for disabled people.

Economy, Business and Consumers
- Competitive, open markets with lighter, smarter regulation; small business rates allowance; tougher action on monopolies and bank practices; stronger consumer protections.
- A green economy: replace Climate Change Levy with a fair carbon tax; at least 10% renewables by 2010; phase out nuclear as plants retire; boost research and innovation; stop public subsidies for arms exports.

Democracy and Rights
- Fair votes: AV+ for Westminster as a first step, STV for local/EU; replace the Lords with an elected Senate; stronger Commons scrutiny and Freedom of Information; devolve more power to nations, regions and councils; local income tax.
- Equality Act covering all forms of discrimination; repeal Section 28; fair, faster asylum with dignity; judicial warrants for surveillance; no ID cards.

Communities, Countryside and Seas
- Brownfield first; recycling to 60%; flood resilience; protect green spaces; support village services; reform CAP/CFP toward sustainability and local co‑management; create a Ministry for Rural Affairs.

Europe, Defence and the World
- Pro‑EU reformer: enlargement, a clear constitution with subsidiarity, transparency; euro entry by referendum at a sustainable rate.
- Ethical internationalism: strengthen UN, ICC and conflict prevention; maintain defence spending with flexible, deployable forces; retain minimum nuclear deterrent while pursuing global disarmament; oppose US NMD.

Funding honesty: 1p for education; 50p top rate funds pensions/NHS; close CGT loopholes for police/transport; green tax shifts offset by cuts elsewhere; Citizen’s Tax Contract for transparency.
